source_text: Ἐπιπόλαιον δὲ καὶ τό· ἤδη γάρ που καὶ ἄνθρωπος ἐπιβουλευόμενός τε καὶ προαισθόμενος ἐὰν προείπῃ τοῖς ἐπιβουλεύουσιν, ἀποτρέπονται καὶ φυλάσσονται· πολλοὶ γὰρ καὶ προαισθομένοις τοῖς ἐπιβουλευομένοις ἐπεβούλευσαν. ἑξῆς ὡσπερεὶ τὸ συμπέρασμα ἐπάγων τῷ λόγῳ φησίν· οὔκουν ἐπειδὴ προείρητο ταῦτα, γέγονεν, ἀδύνατον γάρ· ἀλλ᾿ ἐπειδὴ γέγονε, ψεῦδος ἐλέγχεται τὸ προειρηκέναι· πάντῃ γὰρ ἀμήχανον τοὺς προακούσαντας ἔτι προδοῦναι καὶ ἀρνήσασθαι. ἀνατραπεῖσι δὲ τοῖς προειρημένοις συνανετράπη καὶ τὸ συμπέρασμα τό· (οὐκ) ἐπεὶ προείρητο ταῦτα, γέγονε. φαμὲν δ᾿ οτι καὶ γέγονεν, ὡς δυνατὸν, καὶ ἐπεὶ γέγονεν. ἀληθὲς δείκνυται τὸ προειρηκέναι· τὸ γὰρ περὶ μελλόντων ἀληθὲς ταῖς ἐκβάσεσι κρίνεται. ψεῦδος οὖν τὸ ὑπ᾿ αὐτοῦ οὕτως εἰρημένον. ὅτι ψεῦδος ἐλέγχεται τὸ προειρηκέναι, καὶ μάτην λέλεκται τῷ Κέλσῳ τό· πάντῃ γὰρ ἀμήχανον τοὺς προακούσαντας ἔτι προδοῦναι καὶ ἀρνήσασθαι.
pass_a_gloss: Superficial (ἐπιπόλαιος) also this: 'for surely already (ἤδη που) even a man being plotted against (ἐπιβουλεύω) and perceiving beforehand (προαισθάνομαι), if he foretells to those plotting, they turn back (ἀποτρέπω, mid.) and are on guard (φυλάσσω, mid.)'. For many plotted even against those plotted-against who perceived beforehand. Next, as if adding the conclusion (συμπέρασμα) to the argument, he says: 'Therefore not because (ἐπειδή) these things had been foretold did they happen, for [that is] impossible (ἀδύνατον); but since they happened, the foretelling (τὸ προειρηκέναι) is exposed (ἐλέγχω) as false (ψεῦδος); for it is wholly impossible (ἀμήχανον) for those who heard beforehand (προακούω) still to betray and deny.' With the premises (τὰ προειρημένα) overturned (ἀνατρέπω), the conclusion is overturned with them (συνανατρέπω): '(not) because these things had been foretold did they happen'. We say that they both happened, as [being] possible (δυνατόν), and since they happened the foretelling is shown (δείκνυμι) true; for the true about future things (μέλλοντα) is judged (κρίνω) by the outcomes (ἐκβάσεις). False therefore what was said by him thus, that the foretelling is exposed as false; and in vain (μάτην) was said by Celsus: 'for it is wholly impossible for those who heard beforehand still to betray and deny.'
pass_b_english: Superficial too is this remark: “For surely even when a man who is being plotted against learns of it in advance and tells the plotters beforehand, they give it up and are on their guard.” For many have plotted even against people who had learned of the plot in advance.

Next, as though drawing the conclusion of his argument, he says: “So it was not because these things had been foretold that they happened, for that is impossible; but since they happened, the foretelling is proved false. For it is altogether impossible that those who had heard beforehand should still betray and deny.” But once his premises have been overturned, the conclusion is overturned with them: “It was not because these things had been foretold that they happened.” We say that these things both happened, as things that could happen, and that, since they happened, the foretelling is shown to be true; for truth about things to come is judged by the outcome. False, then, is what he said in these terms, that the foretelling is proved false; and Celsus has said to no purpose: “For it is altogether impossible that those who had heard beforehand should still betray and deny.”

choices.why: 'they turn back' -> 'they give it up' (ἀποτρέπονται: they desist)
'since it was possible' -> 'as things that could happen' (ὡς δυνατόν)

choices.term: τὸ περὶ μελλόντων ἀληθὲς ταῖς ἐκβάσεσι κρίνεται
choices.why: 'what is said about the future is judged true by the outcome' -> 'truth about things to come is judged by the outcome' (τὸ περὶ μελλόντων ἀληθὲς ταῖς ἐκβάσεσι κρίνεται)

choices.term: his claim, put in these terms
choices.why: 'his claim, put in these terms' -> 'what he said in these terms'

translator_notes: The staged text has (οὐκ) in angle-bracket sense, an editorial supplement in Celsus’s repeated conclusion; read with it, since it repeats the ‘not because’ of the conclusion just quoted. Staged punctuation puts full stops at ‘ἐπεὶ γέγονεν.’ and ‘εἰρημένον.’; read as one sentence each (‘since they happened the foretelling is shown true’; ‘false is what he said, that the foretelling is proved false’). Typo οτι for ὅτι read. ἀποτρέπονται καὶ φυλάσσονται taken as middle with the plotters as subject (‘they turn back and are on their guard’). No Scripture quoted.
